newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Turkey's Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller refused last night to withdraw Ankara's threat of war against Greece and to accept an EU Council decision, effectively ending any possibility of dialogue with Greece. Athens, on its side, refused to lift its reservations on the financing protocol for Turkey, with Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos insisting that Ankara needed to prove its respect for international treaties.
--The union movement appears to be fragmenting into more and more factions: Labour Day celebrations tomorrow will force workers to choose between three different rallies.
--Greece's national carrier Olympic Airways cabin staff are threatening to hold a 24-hour strike tomorrow. The final decision will be taken today. ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Pangalos and Ciller met yesterday in Luxembourg and agreed on the establishment of committees of experts on Greek-Turkish relations.
--Some 400,000 people will have their subsidies and compensation payments from the agricultural sector cut if they receive more than 140 daily wages from other sectors.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis will chair a meeting today on the government's positions on social dialogue to begin with unions and employers soon.

--Greece banks are the most expensive to deal with after Germany's, according to a recent survey. Greece's bank lending and deposit interest rates have a difference of 6.2 percentage points (Germany has 7.3), while the difference in EU member-states, the US and Japan is no more than 2.0.
--Applications for compensation due to adverse weather conditions will be restricted to certain categories of farmers, the agriculture ministry has decided.

--This generation of workers is facing having to deal with a social security system that will be unable to meet its obligations if drastic measures are not taken soon. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
